meta.scope: Guyana batch 4 (final dig) — Power sector (GPL, gas-to-energy), infrastructure boom (roads, bridges, housing), public investment scale, and remaining social/energy nodes. Brings Guyana to solid intermediate–deep coverage.

candidates.title: Guyana Power and Light (GPL)
candidates.description: State-owned vertically integrated electricity utility. Serves the large majority of grid-connected customers; peak demand has roughly doubled with the oil-driven construction and commercial boom.
candidates.notes: Core power-system node. Customer base and peak demand have risen sharply (peak demand from ~120 MW in 2020 toward 200+ MW); capacity additions and the forthcoming gas-to-energy project are the main responses.

candidates.title: Gas-to-Energy project (Wales)
candidates.description: Associated-gas pipeline and combined-cycle power plant project intended to bring offshore gas ashore for domestic power generation and to lower electricity costs.
candidates.notes: Strategic energy-transition node. Continuously cited as the main near-term solution to high-cost, fuel-oil-based generation and as a link between the oil sector and domestic industrial potential.

candidates.title: Housing programme / housing development
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Housing / Government of Guyana
candidates.description: Large-scale public housing and house-lot allocation programme. One of the most visible uses of oil-financed public investment on the coast.
candidates.notes: Lived boom indicator. Budget allocations for housing are among the largest functional lines; new schemes and construction are transforming the coastal landscape around Georgetown and secondary towns.

candidates.title: Roads, bridges and transport infrastructure
candidates.description: National programme of road, bridge and corridor investment (coastal highways, Linden–Lethem, hinterland roads, river transport). Major oil-financed capital expenditure.
candidates.notes: Physical integration node. Continuously cited as the attempt to link hinterland and coastal markets and to support the construction and logistics boom.

candidates.title: Public investment programme
candidates.description: Overall public capital expenditure financed increasingly by NRF withdrawals. Encompasses energy, transport, housing, health and education infrastructure.
candidates.notes: Aggregate fiscal-impulse node. Budget size has multiplied since the start of oil production; capital spending is the primary channel through which oil revenue enters the domestic economy.

candidates.title: EITI / extractive-sector transparency
candidates.description: Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative reporting and related disclosure of oil, gas and mining revenues and payments.
candidates.notes: Governance counterpart to the NRF. Continuously cited in discussions of revenue transparency and accountability in the oil era.

candidates.title: Foreign direct investment statistics
candidates.publisher: Bank of Guyana / Bureau of Statistics
candidates.description: FDI flows and stocks. Dominated by oil-sector investment (ExxonMobil consortium and related service companies); non-oil FDI is smaller but rising with construction and services.
candidates.notes: External-investment counterpart of the production boom. Continuously cited in balance-of-payments and growth analysis.

candidates.title: Region 10 (Upper Demerara-Berbice) — Linden industrial/mining
candidates.description: Interior region centred on Linden. Historic bauxite and industrial centre; gateway corridor toward the deeper hinterland (Linden–Lethem).
candidates.notes: Secondary industrial and transport node. Completes the set of major regions beyond the pure coastal core and the deep hinterland.

candidates.title: Water and sanitation access
candidates.publisher: Guyana Water Inc. / Bureau of Statistics
candidates.description: Household access to improved water and sanitation. Coastal coverage is higher; hinterland and riverain gaps remain material.
candidates.notes: Basic-services node. Continuously cited alongside electricity as a constraint on living standards outside the best-served coastal areas.

candidates.title: Amaila Falls hydropower (project)
candidates.description: Long-planned large hydropower project in the interior. Intended long-run renewable complement to gas-to-energy and thermal generation.
candidates.notes: Long-horizon energy node. Continuously cited as the major renewable option for eventual surplus power and industrialisation; implementation has faced repeated delays.

proposed_edges.basis: Gas-to-energy is the main near-term capacity and cost-reduction project for the GPL system.
Housing is one of the largest functional lines within the public investment programme.
Roads and bridges form a major component of capital expenditure.
NRF withdrawals are the primary financing source of the expanded public investment programme.
EITI reporting covers the same extractive revenues that flow into the NRF.
FDI flows appear in the financial account of the balance of payments.
Linden / Region 10 is the historic centre of bauxite activity.
Water and sanitation gaps are most pronounced in hinterland and riverain communities.
